maya: quick thread — ran a perf sweep on multi-region prefix cache after the kernel-selection change. Noticed a cold-region miss spike in ap-south at ~03:12 UTC. Hit-rate dropped ~38% vs eu-west for same prefix distribution (eu ~62% vs ap ~24%). sample traces below, keeping it short before I open a ticket.

maya: logs snippet: 
```
[03:12:03] request_id=rx9 model=redwood-3b prefix_hash=abc123 region=ap-south cache_lookup=miss routing=local kernel=gemm_fused batch=16
[03:12:04] request_id=rxA model=redwood-3b prefix_hash=abc124 region=ap-south cache_lookup=miss routing=local kernel=gemm_fused batch=8
[03:12:05] request_id=rxB model=redwood-3b prefix_hash=abc123 region=eu-west cache_lookup=hit routing=global kernel=gemm_fused batch=16
```

maya: quick hypothesis: cache key entropy increased because we upstreamed conversation/streaming ids into the key in the hot path (was intended for debugging). eu-west had warmed KV from steady traffic; ap-south didn't because keys differ. Also kernel-selection change bumped default batch sizes which increases prefix fragmentation.

ben: can you paste the current key function?

maya: current (simplified):
```python
def cache_key(model, tenant, prefix, convo_id, seq):
    return sha1(f"{model}:{tenant}:{convo_id}:{seq}:{prefix}")
```

maya: root cause: convo_id+seq in key -> near-unique keys for streaming, prefix reuse destroyed. we intended convo_id only for traceability but streaming path included seq.

gabi: ouch. two quick mitigations: 1) normalize key to remove seq and cap convo_id to short hash, 2) eager-replicate top-100k prefixes between regions and run a priming job.

sam: on kernel/batching side — for cold-region traffic switch kernel selection policy to favor smaller batch target (batch=4) and prioritize lightweight kernels so first-token latency doesn't spike while cache warms. that reduces prefix fragmentation because we coalesce smaller batches earlier.

maya: agree. propose changes:
- immediate rollback of seq-from-key in streaming hotpath (hotfix)
- short canary that normalizes key: cache_key = f"{model}:{tenant}:{prefix_hash[:16]}"
- schedule priming job: replay top N prefixes from global telemetry into ap-south with low-priority pods
- routing tweak: route cold-region prefix misses to nearest region with warm cache (prefer cost-tiered routing) for 15m after miss

infra-bot: scheduled job created: priming-job/ap-south-top100k (priority=low) — starts in 10m. ci: https://ci.example/prime/1234

ops-bot: note: we added prefix normalization in the dedicated path last quarter; streaming path was missed (tracked as ENG-4721).

ben: any perf regression risk from removing convo_id/seq? are we losing any correctness guarantees?

maya: no correctness impact — those fields were only for debugging logs. we'll keep them in telemetry but not in the key. We'll add a migration header so older cache entries remain valid for TTL (12h).

gabi: metrics to watch: per-region prefix hit-rate, first-token latency p50/p95, kernel load time, batch size distribution. target is +20% hit-rate in ap-south within 24h, p95 latency <= baseline + 10ms.

sam: I'll prepare a kernel-policy patch that flips to small-batch for region=ap-south when region_hit_rate < 40%. simple config flag to canary it.

maya: will open short RFC and attach canary dashboard. I will also add a small unit test that ensures streaming path doesn't stamp seq into key.

maya: plan of action (TL;DR):
- hotfix: strip seq from key (deploy in next 30m)
- priming job: infra scheduled (starts +10m)
- canary routing + kernel tweak: ben/sam to land config and roll out to 10% traffic for ap-south
- follow-up: monitor and reassess in 24h, then decide on eager replication TTL option

ben: sounds good. ping me when hotfix is up. :thumbsup:

maya: will do. thanks all.
